note: Obligations that cannot be assessed from cloud configuration. An admin records who owns each control and the evidence for it; PolicyGuard tracks the owner, the evidence, the date and when the review is due. It does not judge whether the evidence is good enough. 'basis' says where each control comes from and how well that wording has been verified.

controls.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC or NPL time sources
controls.evidence_hint: For example the time-sync configuration of your servers (Amazon Time Sync or chrony) and a note on how it stays traceable to NIC or NPL.
controls.basis: CERT-In Direction (i); FAQ Q40 to Q42 allow native cloud time services.

controls.title: Point of contact designated and sent to CERT-In (Annexure II)
controls.evidence_hint: Name of the contact and the date the details were sent to CERT-In.

controls.title: Procedure to report Annexure I incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours
controls.evidence_hint: A link to the runbook, and who can file the report. The Incidents page tracks the 6-hour clock.

controls.title: Log sources in scope are listed and kept 180 days
controls.evidence_hint: The list of ICT systems whose logs are kept (for example firewall, IPS, SIEM, web, database, mail, SSH, VPN and application logs) and where.
controls.basis: CERT-In Direction (iv); FAQ Q37 lists example log types.

controls.title: Notice given to people before personal data is collected
controls.evidence_hint: A link to the notice shown to data principals.
controls.basis: DPDP Act section 5 (section number from memory; the Act text was not retrieved).

controls.title: Consent is obtained and can be withdrawn
controls.evidence_hint: How consent is collected and withdrawn, and where it is recorded.
controls.basis: DPDP Act section 6 (not verified against the Act text).

controls.title: Verifiable parental consent for children's data, or a statement that none is processed
controls.evidence_hint: The method used, or a statement that no data of children is processed.
controls.basis: DPDP Act section 9; the PIB explainer mentions verifiable parental consent.

controls.title: Contact point and grievance process published, and requests answered within 90 days
controls.evidence_hint: The published contact and the process for access, correction and erasure requests.
controls.basis: PIB explainer: a contact must be shown and requests answered within ninety days (the Act text was not retrieved).

controls.title: Contracts with data processors include security safeguards
controls.evidence_hint: The processor contracts or the standard clause used.
controls.basis: DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 6(1)(f), from a third-party reproduction of the rule text.

controls.title: Significant Data Fiduciary duties assessed (audit, impact assessment) or marked not applicable
controls.evidence_hint: The assessment, or a note that the organisation has not been designated.
controls.basis: PIB explainer: audits and impact assessments apply to Significant Data Fiduciaries.

controls.title: Breach intimation procedure: Board without delay, detailed report within 72 hours, affected people informed
controls.evidence_hint: The runbook and who sends each notice. The Incidents page tracks the clocks.
controls.basis: DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 7, from a third-party reproduction of the rule text.

controls.title: Personal data is erased when its purpose is served or consent is withdrawn
controls.evidence_hint: How deletion is triggered and checked. The lifecycle check only shows a rule exists.
controls.basis: DPDP Act section 8(7) (not verified against the Act text).

controls.title: Transfers of personal data outside India reviewed
controls.evidence_hint: The review of data stored or processed outside India and the sector rules that apply.
controls.basis: DPDP Act section 16 (not verified); sector rules may be stricter.
